gloss: to run all the way; to finish running

definitions.gloss: to run all the way (to the end); to finish running a distance
definitions.explanation: To run from start to finish without stopping, completing the entire intended distance. Emphasizes seeing the run through to its end rather than the speed or quality of running.

examples.japanese: ゴールまで{走|はし}り{切|き}った。
examples.english: I ran all the way to the goal.

examples.japanese: {最後|さいご}まで{走|はし}り{切|き}る{自信|じしん}がない。
examples.english: I don't have the confidence to run the whole distance.

examples.japanese: {途中|とちゅう}で{足|あし}が{痛|いた}くなったが、なんとか{四十二|よんじゅうに}キロを{走|はし}り{切|き}ることができた。
examples.english: My legs started to hurt partway, but I somehow managed to run the whole 42 kilometers.

notes:
Compound of {走|はし}る (to run) + {切|き}る (to finish completely, used as a suffix). The 〜{切|き}る ending adds the meaning of doing something all the way through to completion.

TRANSITIVITY:
Intransitive in basic use ({最後|さいご}まで{走|はし}り{切|き}る), but can take a distance as the object marked with を ({四十二|よんじゅうに}キロを{走|はし}り{切|き}る).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ゴールまで{走|はし}り{切|き}る: run all the way to the goal
- {最後|さいご}まで{走|はし}り{切|き}る: run to the very end
- フルマラソンを{走|はし}り{切|き}る: complete a full marathon

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {走|はし}り{抜|ぬ}く: run all the way through — emphasizes determination and pushing past difficulty
- {完走|かんそう}する: complete a race — formal, used for organized events
